question: Which infection causes the destruction of T cells in the body?
answer: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) is the infection that causes the destruction of T cells in the body. It specifically targets CD4+ T cells, which are crucial for the immune system's response to infections. Over time, HIV can deplete these cells, leading to AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) if left untreated.
ground_truth: Both types of HIV destroy T cells in the body. These T cells are critical in helping your body fight disease; when these T cells are destroyed, your body becomes ‘immunocompromised’ or more susceptible to other diseases.
